prize_parts.citation: For developing targeted protein degradation by induced proximity, through heterobifunctional PROTACs and the identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide-type molecular glue degraders

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is the one candidate that most of the committee ranks highly, three of us first. The chemical idea is original and general: a small molecule that brings an E3 ligase and a target into one ternary complex, so that degradation becomes a designable event rather than inhibition. The mechanism is supported by crystal structures of ternary complexes and by cell biology from many independent labs, which is the kind of structural evidence I look for. Handa's identification of cereblon explains why thalidomide analogues work and gives a structural and mechanistic basis for the molecular glue strand. Crews and Deshaies give the conceptual origin. The result is a new therapeutic modality with a clear molecular rationale and a growing clinical pipeline.
statement.case_against: Clinical validation is incomplete: as far as I know no PROTAC has been approved, so the prize would rest on mechanism and concept rather than on a delivered medicine. The field is also two partly distinct discoveries, PROTACs and cereblon-mediated glues, and any three names leave out Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and Ito, whose claims are real. A prize that tries to cover both strands risks a citation that is too broad or credits that look arbitrary. My own first choice, ordered mesoporous silica (B005), is a cleaner and more mature story but has no support from any colleague, and I do not think that should be mistaken for a lack of merit or forced into consensus.

responses.point: Aili ranks B019 first with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, arguing that it gives a general molecular design principle and that Handa's cereblon work explains molecular-glue degraders and the clinical IMiD story.
responses.response: I agree with this configuration and with the logic of including Handa. Cereblon is a structurally defined target, and without it the glue strand has no mechanism. I do not accept that the clinical status is a mere detail: some degraders are in late-stage trials, but I would want the citation to be phrased around the chemical principle so that the prize does not depend on a specific approval. I also question your ranking of base editing second. Liu is the clear driver, but the 2020 CRISPR prize makes the chemistry-specific contribution harder to defend, and the credit question for Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida is unresolved.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks B019 first but takes Ciulli as the third laureate, giving Ciulli credit for VHL ligands and mechanistic and structural rigor, and regards the molecular-glue arm as a competing credit stream.
responses.response: This is the real disagreement on B019. I accept that Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex crystal structures are exactly the structural, rational-design work I value, and I considered him seriously. I still prefer Handa, because cereblon is a discovery of a molecular target that opened a whole therapeutic class, while VHL ligand design is a major advance inside the PROTAC framework Crews and Deshaies established. If the committee wants a PROTAC-only citation, I could accept Ciulli. If it wants to recognise the mechanism of thalidomide, Handa is needed, and I would not drop the glue strand just because it is hard to fit.

responses.point: Somfai ranks Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B034) first as a general, widely used bond-forming method, but asks what is chemically new in targeted degradation and worries that recognition may be premature without an approved drug.
responses.response: The question about what is chemically new is fair. The answer is not a new reaction, it is a new design principle: bifunctional recognition elements and ligand chemistry that make an E3 ligase act on a chosen target. That is more than a biological observation. I do not share your worry about timing to the same degree, since mechanism and independent confirmation are strong. On B034, I respect the adoption, but I rank it outside my top eight because the 2010 cross-coupling prize covers the same transformation class and Kosugi's earlier work clouds priority, so the novelty relative to prior recognition seems lower than for degradation.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks long-range protein electron transfer (B055) first and nitrogenase second, valuing physical-mechanism and structural studies of bioenergetic chemistry, and he places B019 seventh because no PROTAC is approved and the glue and PROTAC strands may need separate recognition.
responses.response: I share your emphasis on mechanism and structural evidence, and that is why I kept nitrogenase (B046) in my top eight with Rees, Einsle and Seefeldt. But I keep it below B019 because, as you say yourself, the N2 reduction mechanism is not settled, so a prize would honour structure and cofactor chemistry rather than the central question. For B055, my concern is the one you raise: the Marcus prize of 1992 may already cover the conceptual core, so I would need a clear argument that the protein experiments are a distinct discovery. On B019 I agree that the two strands are distinct, but I think the cereblon work is what makes a single prize coherent, because it shows both strands act through E3 ligase recruitment.

responses.point: Linke ranks nanopore sensing (B002) first as a clean physical principle that became a commercial single-molecule sequencing technology, and ranks B019 fourth because clinical validation is incomplete.
responses.response: Nanopore sensing has the strongest maturity case on the list, and I agree it creates a real new capability. My hesitation is attribution: five credited names, uncertainty about who is eligible, and a real question whether the decisive step is the 1996 translocation, pore engineering or enzyme ratcheting. I also see it as nearer to biophysics and instrumentation than to chemistry. I would not rule it out, but I would want the committee to agree on a defensible trio before ranking it above B019, and I do not think your trio of Kasianowicz, Deamer and Akeson resolves Bayley's role.

uncertainties: Whether the third laureate on B019 should be Handa (cereblon and the molecular glue strand) or Ciulli (VHL ligands and structure-guided PROTAC design).
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC drug is a reason to wait one more year.
Whether ordered mesoporous silica (B005) can gain any support among colleagues, and whether Ryoo, Inagaki, Stucky or Zhao is the right third name beside Kresge and Beck.
I am relying on memory of the history of several of these fields and have not verified priority details.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent for B019. For B005 and B006 my own work on porous materials and electron crystallography is close to the subject, which is a scientific closeness rather than a personal tie, but I note it for transparency. I have no known personal or institutional link to the named candidates, and Stockholm University colleagues (including Secretary Brzezinski) are not candidates.
